mutant.expected: rc non-zero. The SEDOL limb is what stops a genuine SEDOL being rewritten into a CUSIP, so disarming it must be detected by a suite that claims to prove the limb load-bearing.

It also located exactly which assertion carries the SEDOL limb's weight: section 5, the constructed-collision exhibit, reported 'no collision found; this section is vacuous and must not be read as a pass' -- the suite refuses to pass vacuously when the limb it probes is gone. FINDING WORTH CARRYING: sections 1-4 and 6 STILL PASSED under the mutant, INCLUDING 'ICT 6455819 untouched' and 'MER B247XZ6 untouched'. Both are refused by the CUSIP limb independently, because neither one's zero-padding satisfies the CUSIP check digit, so both survive with the SEDOL check fully disarmed. The SEDOL limb protects the CLASS of future collisions: values that are valid SEDOLs AND whose padding passes the CUSIP check, which the suite has to CONSTRUCT (BBB0135, BBB0168, BBB0317, BBB0481, BBB0630) because no live holding is one today. So the live data cannot exercise the SEDOL limb at all and only the constructed exhibit can. RTX (7.55E+105) is the same vendor class by a different mechanism: the sheet read the E as a scientific-notation exponent and rounded the mantissa, so the identifier is DESTROYED rather than shortened and no padding reconstructs it. Both pass through verbatim and the DEPLOYED bytes were confirmed to do so.
